reviews.text: So sad when vets get very unfriendly once they do great business. I've taken three dogs to Dr. Hershey and she was great with all of them. Now, you have to drop your pet off and leave them ALL DAY and then she will work them in. Why? If someone has a severely anxious dog, that does NOT work. Amazing how quickly the quality of care and compassion go out the window once someone gets busy.

Reading this means you are doing something hard, you are caring for your companion in a way that no one else will, and you are trying to make a hard decision. Integrative Veternary Oncology assisted me in a time when I felt overwhelmed and unsure of the future for my important friend. They provided me with compassionate guidance, clear information, and support that helped me navigate the difficult choices I faced. Their expertise and empathy made a significant difference in my journey, and I am grateful for their assistance during such a challenging time.

Anubis ultimately passed, but the care I received from IVO made me feel some level of control at a time where I felt powerless. They gave me a few extra moments with Anubis, and for that, I will always be thankful. The team at Integrative Veterinary Oncology not only helped me make informed decisions but also provided emotional support that was invaluable. Their dedication to both the patient and the pet owner is truly commendable. I highly recommend their services to anyone facing similar challenges with their beloved pets.

Dr Hershey saved my dog and gave him an additional two years of life, when all other vets said he had "three months" due to his type of cancer. I am eternally grateful Dr. Hershey and her clinic were a part of my life, and more importantly my dog's life. Our dog has passed on due to old age (the all dogs should), and wouldn't have made it at all if it weren't for Dr. Hershey, let alone an additional two years. Thank you Dr. Hershey.
It's been a while I forgot to rate years ago but they helped us with my boy Duke. Can't praise them enough.

Our small mixed breed service dog diagnosed w Lymphoma a month ago and we were recommended here. They got us in, stating priority for lymphoma due to aggressive status on this cancer. They have been friendly, kind, informative and on time w updates and care. Our dog doesn't even mind coming, she wags her tail and prances in like it's no big deal. She doesn't even do this at her regular vet.

My beloved cat Pudge just started treatment with Dr. Hershey at Integrative Vet Oncology for a recurring mast cell tumor.  I couldn't be happier with the timely and effective treatment plan.  His tumor is very close to his eye, but the side effects from the Electrochemotherapy treatments are minimal, and after 2-3 visits I look forward to having my healthy, happy cat back again.  Without a cone! Many, many thanks to Dr. Hershey and her exceptional team.

Dr. Hershey is absolutely amazing!

My “vet” recommended me to a surgeon originally and instead I took my fur baby here!
No referral needed! I will recommend getting all your pets records sent to you prior since the “vet” never forwarded Hersheys office my dogs records, X-rays, bloodwork, etc.

She assessed the situation and told me ALL of my options, realistically. I wanted facts and she provided them each and every time. Every time my dog came in there she loved the staff!

I honestly feel that Hershey gave me extra months with my dog and the treatment plan we chose. I also feel that they never overcharged m/upsold me for anything, like some places will do when you’re in a vulnerable position.

Anytime I called, a staff member was very quick to call me back. I felt that they truly cared about my dog, as patient, and me, as a worried dog mom.

If your dog has cancer, a tumor, I would HIGHLY recommend coming here first before going to a surgeon.

Here’s some photos of my baby girl in their office. So happy to be there and clearly you can see her favorite spot
They got my in right away & they been taking care on my beautiful baby boy. Thank you to doc & her wonderful staff. I can't thank you enough.

We cannot thank Dr. Hershey and the entire oncology team enough for the care they gave our Billie. When she was diagnosed with osteosarcoma, we were determined to give her every opportunity and every good day possible. Her CT was clear, her amputation went beautifully, and she handled her first chemotherapy incredibly well. Despite all of that, just a few months after her 5th birthday, her journey ended far sooner than any of us expected when her body simply could not keep going.

Billie was a once in a lifetime dog; a gentle giant who helped hundreds of foster dogs and cats find their footing and, ultimately, their forever homes. One of the many reasons we chose IVO was their commitment to rescue and the work they do to help animals in need. It felt only fitting that a team so dedicated to giving animals a second chance would be the ones caring for our Billie.

Throughout every step, the compassion, professionalism, and genuine care shown by the doctors and technicians meant the world to us. They checked on her after hours, celebrated her victories with us, and grieved alongside us when we lost her. The memorial tree they planted in her honor was an incredibly thoughtful gesture that we will never forget.

As a veterinarian myself, I have a deep appreciation for what high-quality medicine and client care should look like, and this team exceeded every expectation. More importantly, as a pet parent who loved Billie beyond words, I always knew she was in the best hands possible.

Billie was deeply loved, and we are so grateful to everyone who helped us make the most of the time we had with her. We all miss her dearly. Thank you for your kindness, dedication, and for treating her like one of your own. When the inevitable need arises in the future, I will trust this team with my pets again without hesitation. ❤️
Got the answers, clearly, that I needed. Everyone was very helpful. Expensive, for me, but worth it, to be able to move forward with my dogs care.

I was referred by another vet because my dog has a mast cell tumor. I read reviews and do research before taking my dog anywhere. There were a couple very positive reviews for the same breed dogs with similar situations. I read some negative reviews from others as well. I can say that I am extremely happy with my experience.

My dog had a large mass about the size of a baseball and he was very uncomfortable. I called and spoke to Lori in reception and she was so nice. She answered all of my questions and gave me suggestions.
I also talked to Brie a couple of times trying to book an appt. They are really busy but definitely worth the wait.

My first appointment was 4 days ago and I was really worried about my dog's health. I brought him in early in the morning and the place is very nice inside. I met Lori and checked in and commented on how nice it smells there. I've had dogs my whole life and been to many vet offices. This place is clean. The reception area is large and nicely decorated. Nice comfortable couches to sit in while dropping off or picking up your pet.

The girl that came out to take my dog was very sweet and he instantly went to her. She said hello and took his leash and away he went without looking back. I drove home and received a call from the vet around noon. The vet gave me the prognosis and pricing for treatment. They did his first chemo that afternoon and he was very cheerful and seemed like he was in no visible pain when I picked him up at 5pm. I saw several people dropping off and picking up dogs there and everyone seemed to be very happy with their experience.

Doctor Hershey came out to greet me and she was very kind and personable. You can tell she really loves what she does. I can't imagine what happened to make someone give a negative review. Everyone here is amazing!

My dog's mass has already shrunk down by half or more in the 4 days since we were first there. He has another appointment in 3 days for a second chemo and my fears have all been replaced by optimism. I know this was the right place to take him and I'm very thankful to Dr Hershey and her staff for the great care they have given and the peace of mind they've instilled in me. This has been a stressful ordeal and everyone there has made it possible to breathe easy knowing we're in great hands.

I can’t say enough positive about DR HERSHEY &  her team !  She’s amazing. The care, the commitment and dedication to our dogs health is unmatched! The office when you walk in feels like a living room and the dogs feel it when they walk in. Lori & Bre that work the front are sweet and take care of your pet like their own . I prayed we would get in this office and so happy we did !

I cannot say enough wonderful things about Dr. Hershey and the rest of the staff. They provide state of the art cancer care, but additionally are warm and welcoming. They are also easy to get a hold of for questions that come up. Thank you for all you do!

From the moment we received the devastating diagnosis in December of 2024 that our precious Baby Boy, Rocco — our “Handsome Dude” — had a high-grade mast cell tumor, our world stopped.

We were overwhelmed, heartbroken, and unsure of what to do next.

That all changed when we connected with Integrative Vet Oncology and Dr. Hershey.
From our very first call, Dr. Hershey brought not only expertise, but a level of compassion and clarity that immediately gave us hope.

She didn’t just present options — she created a plan, a real path forward, tailored specifically for Rocco. Her knowledge, honesty, and genuine care for both Rocco and our family were evident every step of the way.

Because of Dr. Hershey and her incredible team, we were given something we will never be able to repay — time. Not just days or weeks… but an additional 19 months with our boy. Nineteen more months of love, tail wags, early mornings, memories, and moments we will carry with us forever.

Her staff was just as amazing — always responsive, kind, and supportive. During some of our hardest days, they were steady, professional, and deeply compassionate. You can feel that they truly care about the animals and families they serve.

Rocco passed on April 24, 2026, and while losing him is one of the hardest things we’ve ever gone through, we find peace in knowing we did everything we could — and that we had the best possible team fighting alongside us.

If you are facing a diagnosis like this, know that Integrative Vet Oncology and Dr. Hershey are the people you want in your corner. They don’t just treat the disease — they care for your pet and your family as a whole.

We will forever be grateful.

Thank you, Dr. Hershey and team, for giving us more time with our Handsome Dude. That is something we will cherish for the rest of our lives.

My 8 year old dog suddenly got a very aggressive form of Lymphoma and within a few days of showing symptoms was in very bad shape. Dr. Hershey’s office was the only one who was able to get me in the same week. Dr. Hershey and her staff are great, I was kept very informed and they got back to me very quickly anytime I had questions throughout her treatment. They also got me in same day (on several occasions) when her treatment stopped working and were able to switch her over to something else.  They were transparent about cost, prognosis and what her quality of life would look like. My dog was never excited to go to the vet but based on how happy she was to see the staff I could tell they treated her very well. Although my sweet Lola didn’t make it, I am grateful for the extra 4 months they gave us.  Thank you ❤️🐶

SAVE YOURSELF THE TRIP. INTEGRATIVE VET ONCOLOGY IS NOT BBB APPROVED.  if you’re doing chemo for your dog please go to medvet Scottsdale. They are amazing. This place on the other hand is TRASH. the building has been their building for 13 years and it’s gross inside. Smells bad. And looks very unsanitary. The lady on the phone is RUDE and will lead you to believe you have an appointment with the doctor when you will not be able to speak to a doctor AT ALL. Unless it’s over the phone once your dog is in their care already. My gut was screaming not to do it. So I didn’t. I am going to medvet. Not only that but take the time to read the reviews of people who have been put through hell with this place. They shouldn’t even be aloud to have a business anymore. Keeping dogs under anesthesia all day. Locking the doors on people. Not keeping updated on the dogs. They have clearly no compassion for the animal and only care about the money. DO NOT DO IT. please take your baby somewhere else. Customer service is terrible. Care is not existent. You won’t be able to speak to a doctor. And lemme repeat myself THE BUILDING IS UNSANITARY. extremely disappointed in the entire experience there and glad I trusted my gut and did NOT leave my dog in their care.
Not very friendly or compassionate

IVO is outstanding!  My dog has had mast cell cancer for well over a year.   When my vet referred me to IVO I was afraid.  The folks at IVO were great; always professional, but very empathetic and willing to answer any questions, even over the phone at later times. The people who work at the front are excellent.  These are women who remember your name and listen when you need to talk.  I just can't say enough.

We have been bringing our 12-year-old cat, Patches, to Dr. Hershey and the team at Integrative Veterinary Oncology for months now to manage her lymphoma. They have always been wonderful, but they truly saved her life this week.

When Patches recently took a sudden turn for the worse and went into respiratory distress, the team didn't make us wait.. they got her in immediately. Thanks to their quick action and aggressive treatment, she went from fighting to breathe to eating and purring within 24 hours. It honestly felt like a miracle.

Beyond the top-tier medical care, I am incredibly grateful for Dr. Hershey’s compassion. She understands the financial reality of long-term cancer treatment and has been so supportive, helping us skip unnecessary expensive diagnostics (like X-rays) so we can put every dollar toward the actual life-saving medication instead.

To the front desk, the techs, and Dr. Hershey: thank you for fighting for her with us. If you need an oncologist who is both skilled and genuinely kind, this is the place.

It has taken me a very long time to right this review because it was such a difficult time. I just feel that it is very important for people to know so they don’t have to go through the same thing we did. My sweet Jazz passed away 1/8/24. We had taken him here to treat his intestinal carcinoma. His visits were very long, we would drop him off in the am and wouldn’t be able to pick him up until the end of the day. Every time I picked him up his blanket was soiled which leaves me to believe they did not take him out during the day. The treatment itself was very short however it was mandatory to leave them all day. In our time there we only met with the Dr Hershey once. Very frequently we were told that they were running late because Dr had come in late. Most times when we dropped him off the staff would make mistakes.Calling Jazz her rather than him, confusing last drop of date, confusing reason for drop off. Staff always seemed annoyed when we called in to check on him. All these things were terrible, however he had already started treatment and we didn’t want to create more issues with helping him.  The heart breaking part came as he was passing. He had finished treatment and we were told that the only option he had was taking oral chemo at this point. We were waiting for genetic testing. ( we were offered to start a random one but we decide to wait for the genetic test to make sure it was the right one. His cancer was controlled, We were not advised that it was detrimental to put him on something right away). The test was sent in late and then also took longer to process with the holiday. During this three week span things started to take a turn for the worst. We had one visit that we made because he wasn’t eatting. They did a scan and saw that his cancer had spread. There was a concern that maybe there was something else going on so they said to wait until result came back to do anything. Very quickly he got very sick. We called numerous times explaining how sick he was and they would not let us come in, nor did we get a call back from the Dr Hershey. Out of desperation we went to an emergency vet. There is little they would do without talking to Dr because of his condition and not getting approval. They reached out to the Dr multiple times, finally the following day she called them back. They put him on a steroid, pain med, and IV. They also gave us instruction on what we could do. They said that we had to go to our dr moving forward for more meds. Dr Hershey never got Jazz back in nor did she call us back until I finally left a message begging and crying. I even saw that his result were in on Friday and she didn’t call until Monday. At that point she said the medication the emergent vet gave was what she would recommend and we would know when  it was time. She also recommend to talk to a animal psychic if we wanted to know when it was his time.  He passed away the next day. He had some very horrible days that could have been prevent if given the right medication in appropriate days, and we could have planned differently had she just seen him and told us what was happening. She gave us hope that possibly it was something else causing the no eating and sickness. They never even called us or emailed us to give us the results of the genetic  testing that we spent something around $1500 for. Until I called and asked for it. We never received any thing more from them. I know we all take our pets to a place like this to get more time, we know it’s not a fix but the most important part is making sure that when they do pass it happens it the most peaceful and painless way. They took that from Jazz and from my family. The last moments were filled with stress, the unknowing, and unnecessary pain. Thank God for the emergency vet that stepped in. The negligence was unexceptable.   That time was very traumatic for my family and my hope is that this does not happen to anyone else. Shame on you integrative vet oncology and Dr. Hershey.
If you have a pet with cancer and you want the best chance for them Dr Hershey at Intergrative Vet Oncology is the one to see.
Dr. Hershey and staff are amazing! Front office staff is kind and helpful. Calls are always returned with useful information! I appreciate all they are doing for our kitty, Phillip Fry.

Doctor Hershey and her staff truly care about my dog. The doctor and staff go above and beyond to make sure my dog, Indie, gets the proper treatment and special care that he needs. And, believe me, Indie is more thsn a handful!! The doctor, and her staff, they make this experience worth the time, trouble and expense.
Do not waste your time with any other oncology veterinarian. This team is best of the best!

They have a Chinese herb that could potentially save my dogs life but they won't sell it to me because I haven't paid for a $300 consult with them that I'd have to wait 6 weeks for. Thankfully Walmart will sell it to me, just have to wait for shipping. Shame on you, IVO.
This place is absolutely amazing. This is my 6 year old who was diagnosed with bone cancer. She is a survivor because of them. Dr Hershey is amazing. All the staff is amazing here

Wonderful caring professionals. Always feel better and both my cancer patients who have been treated there were never afraid or upset to go in - these folks are definitely angels who work miracles through their love and care.  Dr. Hershey is brilliant as well as easy to talk to.

Dr Hershey and the staff took amazing care of our baby girl through her cancer and remission treatment. They have been kind, generous and supportive through Zoe’s journey and I’ll be forever grateful for the 2 and a half extra years we got to love her.
The lady I spoke to wasn't helpful at all. Said appointments were 3 weeks plus out.
Teddy always enjoys his visits here. Never have to drag him in as if he’s expecting something frightening. I  appreciate the thorough discussion with his provider at the end of his exam.

Dr. Hershey is incredibly knowledgeable and compassionate in helping animals, especially mine. What started 2 years ago as a death sentence for my German Shepherd, Pippen, has been and continues to be a success story. After being diagnosed with lymphoma, Pippen was given 2 weeks left to live. That was not an option for us…….so we were referred to Dr. Hershey. We have absolutely no regrets sending our girl for chemotherapy. Pippen has been in remission since her first treatment! We are so blessed to have our girl still with us, all thanks to Dr. Hershey and her amazing team. Every single person there is so kind and so loving towards Pippen! They know us all by name and are so welcoming. Dr. Hershey even came out to my car to meet our newest son that was born. Pippen feels so loved and welcomed when she goes there and I’ve never been disappointed as her mom! We are forever grateful to Dr. Hershey and her team!!!!

I want to preface this review by stating it is not motivated by my dog's death from lymphoma nor is it a general review of all the staff at IVO. I understand my girl had an aggressive form of lymphoma and unfortunately I caught it too late. My consultation with Dr. Venebal was positive and she sat with me, listened to my concerns, and walked me through my options. This review is not targeted at my experience with Dr. Hershey and some of her staff.

I had a deeply disappointing experience at Integrative Veterinary Oncology (IVO) between February and March 2024. My dog, Amber, was diagnosed with lymphoma, and despite the severity of her condition, the care and communication from IVO were severely lacking.

Amber's oncologist, Dr. Hershey, never met with me in person, despite my repeated requests. I started to question was she even on site? Every email response ended in “sent from my iphone.” Each visit was a drop off and pick up,  with different vet techs that couldn’t always answer my questions and advised me to “email the Dr.” Communication was limited to emails, and responses were often delayed and inadequate. My emails and phone calls awaiting a callback were questions about her prescriptions, extreme symptoms that hadn’t been discussed with me, and symptoms that I’d been made aware of and was advised to call immediately if they continued for more than 24 hrs. The clinic staff on the phone were at times curt, adding to the frustration during an stressful time.

Amber underwent 4 chemo treatments, and after each, I received no follow-up call checking on her. My primary vet always follows up to check in, especially after any procedures. Additionally, her white blood cell count was too low for one of her visits to get the assigned chemo, so she was administered a different drug without my consent. One weekend her health declined. I took her to an emergency vet and received more compassionate care than I ever experienced at IVO. They even called me the next day to check in on Amber. IVO never did that. Despite numerous emails and calls for guidance, I received minimal support from IVO.

On Monday 3/21/24, Amber's condition worsened significantly, and I rushed her to an emergency clinic (BluePearl). Her breathing wasn’t normal. IVO wasn’t open yet so I emailed a video of Amber’s breathing, asking desperately for guidance on what to do, and rushed her to the ER.  On the drive to the ER, I received a very transactional phone call from the office staff, informing me that they believe it’s time for me to say goodbye. I received an email from Dr. Hershey advising the same. There was no offer of compassion or offer to bring her to the clinic to say goodbye. I had to make the heartbreaking decision to euthanize Amber at BluePearl.

After Amber passed away, I received no follow-up from IVO. I had an appointment scheduled for her the next day that had not been canceled. Nobody called me. To this day, nobody has called me from IVO. Not even Lori who wanted to correct the poor communication & service I’d received and told me “I’ll be your main point of contact.”  The lack of empathy and care was shocking, especially from a facility specializing in cancer treatment. I truly don’t understand how one can commit their complete career and life to this type of work and forget the people and the animals in the process. I don’t know if the staff is overwhelmed, or why I/Amber didn’t get the proactive care and communication we deserved, especially considering the amount of money I was paying to get her treated. I understand others have had a more positive experience, and that’s great. I hope my experience is in the minority.

I hope sharing my experience helps others avoid the distress and frustration I went through. The poor communication, lack of empathy, and questionable ethics at IVO are deeply concerning, and I would strongly advise seeking care elsewhere for your beloved pets.

Note:  I wrote all of the finer details of my complaints and concerns directly to IVO in an email, so Dr. Hershey is aware of my complaints and feedback.
